newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark sees big German sales ahead.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark sees big German sales ahead.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark said on Wednesday that it expected annual fixed network telephony sales in Germany to reach 600-700 million marks in the year 2001.

"We expect to secure five percent of the market for small and medium-sized businesses in the next four years," Bruno Lund Pedersen, managing director of Tele Danmark's German subsidiary Tele Danmark Internetz GmbH, told Reuters.
"This corresponds to an annual turnover of 600-700 million marks," he said.

Tele Danmark's new German unit is next Tuesday to be licensed to operate fixed-line services in Germany and an interconnect deal is due to be launched with Germany's Deutsche Telekom a week later, Petersen said.

"Our interconnect pact with Deutsche Telekom means that we can use the entire German national network. We intend at first to concentrate on the 40 biggest cities in Germany, our target will be small and medium-size firms," he said.
"The deal allows us to offer domestic and foreign telephony in Germany, similar to the agreement (Sweden's state-owned) Telia has with Tele Danmark in Denmark," Petersen said.

Apart from Tele Danmark Internetz, which is based in Hamburg, the Danish telecoms group's activities in Germany include a 20 percent shareholding in pager firm Miniruf. --Morten Bonde Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969651
